request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change that moves a figure now writes the rollup lines to the audit file. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works:** each endpoint that changes data takes a snapshot of the sheet's figures before the change and another after it, then writes the difference.

- **`rollup/Rollup.java`** works out each person's claimed and due-total, in the order they were added, plus the sheet's totals. It uses the same rules as the screen: only open and settled claims count, a person's due-total can be `n/a`, and `n/a` is skipped in the sheet's due-total. It also builds the audit lines:
  - one `ROLLUP` line per person whose figures changed, or who is new;
  - then one `TOTALS` line, only if the claimed-total or due-total changed.
- **`TakeRollup`** takes the "before" snapshot. It runs first, right after the request is checked.
- **`AuditRollup`** takes the "after" snapshot and writes the lines, after the change's own audit line.

These two steps are wired into all eight change endpoints: rates, today, add person, edit person, add claim, edit claim, claim open/settle/void, and statement. A refused change stops before the after-step, so it writes no rollup lines. Changing today has no audit line of its own, so its rollup lines follow straight after the change. Changes that move nothing write nothing, for example setting a rate to the value it already has.

**One difference from the request's wording:** the request says `ROLLUP name=<name>`, but the test expects `person=<name>`. I used `person=` to match the test.

No front-end or database changes were needed.
